title: Does an Apple After Lunch Really Spike Your Sugar?

scenes.text: Apple after lunch? Does it spike sugar?
Many believe fruit right after a meal causes a big blood‑sugar jump.
scenes.label: Fruit spikes sugar

scenes.text: The fiber in fruit slows digestion, so the overall glucose rise is modest.
scenes.label: Fiber balances glucose

scenes.text: Enjoy fruit with meals – it’s fine for most people.
scenes.label: Fruit is fine
scenes.sub: Fiber keeps the sugar rise gentle

scenes.text: Follow if your body is worth 60 seconds a day.

description: A quick look at why eating fruit after a meal isn’t the blood‑sugar villain it’s made out to be. Stay tuned for more myth‑busting health facts.
